patches.value: For an extended metric space X with its Borel measurable structure and real a, μH[a] denotes the native MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a, defined as mkMetric(r↦r^a). Here mkMetric is the Borel measure associated to the metric outer measure obtained by taking the supremum over positive diameter scales of the outer measures generated by costs on sets of diameter at most that scale. Empty sets have zero cost. This uses the native extended-real-power convention at a=0. Values on arbitrary subsets are outer-measure values. Its explicit countable-cover formula is invoked as a source theorem in the proof.

dim_H(A) is the native Hausdorff dimension dimH A: with the Borel structure it is sup{a : a is a nonnegative real and μH[a](A)=infinity}, where the supremum is taken in [0,infinity] and sup(empty)=0. Thus dim_H(empty)=0. This is the usual Hausdorff dimension. The proof identifies μH with the supplied unnormalized measure H on Euclidean spaces at every positive exponent; the zero exponent can contribute only the value zero to this supremum.
D=dim_H(E), initially an extended nonnegative real. Its finiteness is proved before any use of its real value; after that proof it is identified with the corresponding finite nonnegative real.
